title: Objective Assessment of Upper Extremity Functioning of Stroke Patients Before and After Rehabilitation
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate by objective measures the improvement in upper extremity functioning, as reflection of motor learning, in stroke patients in the sub acute phase. The investigators hypothesize that the improvements in daily functioning are partially due to compensation strategies and partially due to motor learning.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* diagnosis of cerebral stroke with upper extremity hemiparesis
* Ability to understand simple orders

Exclusion Criteria:

* Other orthopedic pathology
* Apraxia
* Bilateral Paresis
* Other neurologic pathology
* sensory aphasia
study_population: Cohort will be selected from Fliman Rehabilitation Geriatric Center. Healthy subjects, age and gender-matched will be served as a control group.
